build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player assigns reporters to story leads by dragging or clicking, with each reporter having skill ratings and specialties that affect story quality. Score 0 if no reporter assignment exists.

A fact-check vs speed tradeoff exists: the player chooses between fast publication (higher error risk, captures readers) and thorough investigation (slower, more accurate). Score 0 if no speed/accuracy tradeoff exists.
Published stories affect reputation (accuracy builds trust, errors damage it) and revenue (readership drives ad income and subscriptions). Score 0 if publishing has no consequence.
The player arranges stories in the edition layout (front page, inside, buried) affecting their impact on readership and reputation. Score 0 if no layout mechanic exists.
Financial management requires balancing reporter salaries, equipment costs, and revenue to avoid bankruptcy, with visible budget tracking. Score 0 if no financial system exists.
At least 5 distinct story categories (politics, crime, sports, business, culture) with different complexity levels and reader interest. Score 0 if only one story type exists.
At least 4 distinct reporter types with different specialties, reliability ratings, and salary demands. Score 0 if all reporters are identical.
Between editions the player can hire/fire reporters, invest in fact-checking tools, or expand coverage areas with at least 4 upgrade options. Score 0 if no between-edition management exists.
The campaign spans 20+ editions with escalating story complexity, competitor pressure, and financial targets. Score 0 if difficulty never increases.
An edition summary shows stories published, accuracy rate, readership change, reputation change, and profit/loss. Score 0 if editions end abruptly with no summary.
Normal startup shows a styled title screen with the game name, newsroom or printing-press themed imagery, and a Start control. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The flow connects title to editor desk to story assignment to edition layout to publication results without restarting the executable. Score 0 if major transitions are missing.

The editor view clearly shows story leads, reporter assignments, edition layout, reputation meter, and financial status in readable non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if the player cannot determine newspaper state.

Player actions produce visible feedback: assigning reporters shows them working, publishing shows the edition, errors trigger correction notices, reputation changes animate, and financial updates flash. Score 0 if actions happen silently.

Art direction is coherent across title, newsroom, stories, reporters, editions, and menus with a consistent newspaper-office palette and style. Score 0 if mostly default controls or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

Reporter portraits, story cards, edition layouts, office furniture, and UI elements use real illustrated art with distinct newspaper-themed designs. Score 0 if primary elements are unstyled rectangles.

Animation brings the newsroom to life: reporters typing, stories developing progress bars, edition printing animation, reputation meter movement, and deadline countdown effects. Score 0 if all elements are static.
HUD and UI panels use styled themed widgets with newspaper column layouts, typewriter fonts, or press-room styling rather than raw HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if all UI is default Label/Button.
